title: Protestant church singing and long funerals
summary: They compare Protestant song books and the length of funerals with the quick Catholic services.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Could I ask you just a little bit about the singing in those churches in New Orleans? Did they line out their songs, did they use song books, or how did they sing those hymns?
Oh yeah, they used song books. They used song books, sing such a thing as Jeremiah God, and In That City, and Abide in Me, you know? Yeah. All that kind of stuff.
These are Catholic churches? No, these are Protestant churches.
They have lots of Protestant churches that have these convocs to play.

We used to like to play for the Catholic church when we, I mean, play a funeral for Catholic church because they didn't stay in there long, no time. Yeah. But you know when you go play for a Protestant church?

Yeah. You're going to spend a whole evening like that. And you can't get out. You see, these were these all day meetings. They had church meetings that were almost as long as the masses and the Lutheran services several hundred years ago. They lasted a whole morning.
But the funerals, the funerals, you go to a funeral and you think nothing to wait in two hours to get out of the church.
Paul Barnes. Oh Lord. Paul told me about one time they had so many preachers there, so they had to wait till the next day to bury them married and close the cemetery. That's right.
That's right. Yeah. I hope they did it.

Oh, what? Good morning. No, we waited the last, long time. Long time, the last one. And did they read telegrams and messages of condolences at the funerals that you went to? No, but many ladies were talking. All ladies. Well, they did this here at the local Methodist church in Lafayette. Not yet. And I was very much impressed by the telegrams and things at the end of the day. Oh, because were they written in a nice style? From people talking about the person who had died, what a fine person. It was this music teacher that I mentioned here. Uh-huh. And she was truly a great person.
